subject: anaesthesia
title: Local anaesthetics: chemistry to LAST rescue

steps.tx: Amides such as lignocaine and bupivacaine clear through the liver while esters such as chloroprocaine clear in plasma, which decides choice in liver failure and pregnancy. Only unbound free drug acts, and **pKa** governs how much ionised drug crosses membranes at tissue pH. Higher **lipid solubility** brings faster onset, longer duration and greater potency, cocaine constricts vessels while most agents dilate them, and true allergy clusters with esters through PABA so **protein binding** and vascularity of the site shape dose limits.
steps.say: Chemistry is the predictor of how each agent behaves in the body. Amides are dependent on liver clearance while esters are broken down in plasma. Only the free unbound fraction is active at sodium channels and pKa controls onset speed. Lipid solubility is the driver of potency and duration while vascularity of the site controls absorption. True allergy is rare and clusters with esters, so pregnancy and liver disease need dose review.

steps.tx: Lignocaine stays the versatile agent for infiltration, airway and antiarrhythmic use, **bupivacaine** gives long potent blocks with higher cardiac risk, and **ropivacaine** with levobupivacaine trades some potency for safer cardiac profiles and motor sparing. Prilocaine risks methaemoglobinaemia, **chloroprocaine** suits short obstetric backs, cocaine uniquely shrinks mucosa for topical use, and articaine suits dental infiltration matched to lean weight caps with labelled syringes.
steps.say: Each agent is known by a signature role that is loved by examiners. Lignocaine covers versatile short cases and airway work while bupivacaine covers long potent blocks, which is the split. Ropivacaine and levobupivacaine are options with safer cardiac profiles and motor sparing. Prilocaine is a cause of methaemoglobinaemia and chloroprocaine is suited to short backs. Cocaine is the topical vasoconstrictor and articaine is used for dental infiltration.

steps.tx: Spinal anaesthesia places drug intrathecally with baricity controlling height, **epidural** dosing stays segmental through catheters with test dose and aspiration checks, and **plexus blocks** such as interscalene, axillary and TAP cover limb and abdominal wall surgery. Topical preparations, intravenous Bier blocks with cuff pain limits, wound infusions, and in plane **ultrasound** spreading with adrenaline tachycardia test doses complete the set with consented risks and a lipid rescue kit ready.
steps.say: Blocks are different in where the drug sits and how far it spreads. Spinal drug is intrathecal with baricity that is the setter of height. Epidural drug is segmental through a catheter with test dose protection that is mandatory. Plexus and TAP techniques are the cover for limb and abdominal wall surgery. Topical, intravenous and wound options are the backup for the gaps. Ultrasound guidance with aspiration checks and consent is what keeps every technique safe.

steps.tx: This image shows a needle between scalene muscles at the **plexus trunks** in the interscalene groove under an **ultrasound probe**. The in plane view keeps the shaft and tip visible beside nerves and vessels before any injection. Confirm spread around trunks with small aliquots, aspirate often, and respect phrenic involvement that makes bilateral blocks unsafe with this **interscalene approach**.
steps.say: This image is a view of the interscalene block that is paired with shoulder surgery. The needle is placed between the scalene muscles at the plexus trunks under ultrasound. The probe view keeps the full shaft in sight so the tip is never advanced blind. Small aliquots with frequent aspiration are the proof of spread around the trunks. Phrenic involvement is the reason that bilateral blocks are unsafe.

steps.tx: Local anaesthetic systemic toxicity starts with tinnitus, metallic taste and agitation, then **seizures** needing oxygenation and benzodiazepine, then refractory bupivacaine **arrest**. Treat toxicity with airway support, seizure control, **lipid emulsion** bolus and infusion rescue, and avoidance of vasopressin and calcium blockers. Pregnancy, acidosis and elderly kidneys lower thresholds, so use ultrasound doses with aspiration, track neurology and cardiac review, and report through registries.
steps.say: Toxicity is a fixed order that is recognised early. Prodrome with tinnitus, metallic taste and agitation is the warning before seizures and refractory arrest. Airway support is given and seizures are stopped with oxygenation and benzodiazepine. Lipid emulsion is the specific rescue with bolus and infusion. Pregnancy, acidosis and old age are lowerers of the threshold, so low ultrasound doses with aspiration are the prevention.
